sentenceSets.sentence: The organization was puissant in the period of its greatest institutional confidence, able to shape outcomes through proximity to decision-makers.

answerChoices.reasoning: Prestige is the regard others hold you in, yet the sentence explains the organization's success by its access to those who decide rather than by admiration.
Money is never mentioned; the channel the sentence names is closeness to decision-makers.
Assertiveness is a manner of pressing one's case, but the sentence credits the organization's position rather than its style.
Being impossible to do without would leave others no alternative, whereas the sentence describes results obtained through nearness and confidence.
Talkativeness does not shape outcomes; the sentence attributes them to access.
Respectability is a matter of standing, not the capacity to move outcomes that the sentence describes.
The period is dated by institutional confidence, not by growth in size.
Venerability comes from long age, but the sentence marks out one particular stretch of the organization's life.
Powerlessness contradicts shaping outcomes at all.
Obscurity cannot coexist with proximity to decision-makers.
A defunct body could not shape outcomes during any period.

sentenceSets.sentence: A puissant north wind drove the fleet onto the shoals before the pilots could bring the ships about.

answerChoices.reasoning: A brisk wind is merely lively, but this one overwhelmed the pilots and put ships on the rocks.
Steadiness describes constancy, while what wrecked the fleet was the wind's overmastering of the crews' efforts.
A contrary wind blows against the intended course, yet the disaster here comes from the crews being unable to counter it at all.
Relentlessness is persistence over a long stretch, but the ships struck before the pilots could even come about.
Cold is not what puts a hull on a shoal.
A shifting, unpredictable wind would not drive a whole fleet steadily onto one hazard.
Noise describes how the wind sounded, while the ships were lost to what it did to them.
Whether the wind came at its usual time says nothing about its overcoming the pilots.
A gentle wind could not drive a fleet onto the shoals.
A faint wind would leave the pilots ample time to come about.
Mild pleasantness cannot describe a wind that wrecked a fleet.

sentenceSets.sentence: Her closing argument was the more puissant for being brief: four sentences, and the jury was back with a verdict in eleven minutes.

answerChoices.reasoning: Eloquence is beauty of expression, but the sentence measures the argument by what it produced: a verdict in eleven minutes.
Concision is the brevity the sentence already names as the cause, so it cannot also be the quality that brevity intensified.
Clarity would make the argument easy to follow, whereas what is recorded is how fast it settled the case.
Poignancy moves an audience to feeling, while this jury was moved to a decision.
Shrewdness is cunning calculation, but four sentences that end deliberation in eleven minutes work by sheer weight.
A technical argument would keep a jury out longer, not bring it back inside a quarter of an hour.
Nothing suggests she spoke unprepared; the sentence stresses how much those four sentences accomplished.
Polish is smoothness of finish, and the jury's speed points instead to the argument's force.
Tedium is ruled out by four sentences and an eleven-minute verdict.
A feeble argument would not bring back a verdict in eleven minutes.
Rambling is contradicted by an argument only four sentences long.
